subject: astronomy
title: Spectra Foundations
welcome_lead: Decode starlight using continuous, emission and absorption spectra.
meta_desc: GCSE Astronomy: types of spectra and OBAFGKM stellar classification.
final_note: Spectra are the fingerprints astronomers use to identify stars.

concepts.def: Smooth rainbow with all wavelengths from a hot solid/dense gas.
Bright lines from a hot low-density gas.
Dark lines on continuous spectrum from cooler gas.
Visible 'surface' layer of a star where light is emitted.
Dark absorption lines in the Sun's spectrum.

walkthroughs.body_html: Continuous: hot solid or dense gas (e.g., filament). Emission: hot thin gas (e.g., nebula). Absorption: cool gas in front of a hot continuous source — gives stellar spectra.
From hottest to coolest: O B A F G K M. Remember 'Oh Be A Fine Girl/Guy Kiss Me'. The Sun is a G2 star, with surface temperature ~5800 K.
Hot O stars appear blue (~30,000 K). G stars like the Sun look yellow-white (~5800 K). Cool M stars look red (~3000 K). Colour is a direct clue to surface temperature.
